subject: Amanda Nunes
title: Is Amanda Nunes retired? Not anymore: she fights Kayla Harrison at UFC 334
answer: No. Amanda Nunes retired in June 2023 after beating Irene Aldana at UFC 289, but she has come back. She challenges women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison in the co-main event of UFC 334 on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York.
body:
Nunes, a former two-division UFC champion, gave up her title and stepped away after the Aldana fight, a unanimous-decision win. She later said she had been burned out and needed time away from the pressure of title defenses. She re-entered the UFC's drug-testing pool in 2025, a required step for a return, and called for a fight with Harrison, her former training partner.

The bout was first planned for UFC 324 in January 2026 but was postponed after Harrison needed neck surgery. It was rebooked for UFC 334, where the main event is Ciryl Gane's first defense of the undisputed heavyweight title against Josh Hokit. UFC 334 early prelims start at 5 p.m. ET, prelims at 7 p.m. ET and the main card at 9 p.m. ET, with the main card on Paramount+ in the U.S.

Nunes has not said what comes after this fight. Asked about her plans, she said that if she wins she will have to "defend the belt," and "then we're going to see."
in_the_news: Amanda Nunes returns from a retirement of more than three years to face Kayla Harrison for the UFC women's bantamweight title at UFC 334 on Nov. 14, 2026.

faq.a: In June 2023, after beating Irene Aldana by unanimous decision at UFC 289.

faq.q: When is Amanda Nunes' next fight?
faq.a: Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, against Kayla Harrison at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. The main card starts at 9 p.m. ET.

faq.q: Why was Nunes vs. Harrison postponed?
faq.a: The fight was first set for UFC 324 in January 2026, but Harrison needed neck surgery.
The main card streams on Paramount+ in the U.S.; early prelims are also on UFC Fight Pass.
